After the communist victory in 1975, tens of thousands of Hmong people fled Laos across the Mekong into Thailand. Many had fought for the CIA in the Laotian Civil War under General Vang Pao, from the secret base at Long Tieng.

The new government hunted those who had fought against it. Refugees lived for years in Thai camps, and many were later resettled in the United States, France and Australia. Some Hmong fighters held out in the Lao jungle for decades.

Hmong Americans now number in the hundreds of thousands, with large communities in California and Minnesota. Compare the Vietnamese boat people of the same years. See also bombing of Laos.
